cards.text: Ezra, a priest and scribe, is telling this one himself. After everything's been done, the leaders come to him about the people of Israel and the peoples living all around them. And they've got that "got a minute?" look, and NOBODY who says "got a minute?" only needs a minute.

cards.question: The leaders tell Ezra that the people of Israel haven't done something with the surrounding peoples. What haven't they done?
The leaders tell Ezra that even the priests and Levites are caught up in this.

cards.text: The leaders say these surrounding peoples have abominations like those of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians and more. Friend, the leaders are NOT easing into this one.

cards.question: So what have the Israelites done with these surrounding peoples?
The leaders report that the leaders and officials stayed out of this unfaithfulness.

cards.text: The leaders call it the holy seed being mixed with the people of the land. Then the report lands on Ezra, and friend, it hits him HARD.

cards.question: When Ezra hears the leaders' report, he tears his tunic and cloak.

cards.text: Ezra pulls out some hair from his head and beard, and he sits down in horror. I grabbed my mustache with BOTH hands just reading that.

cards.question: Because of the exiles' unfaithfulness, people start gathering around Ezra as he sits in horror. Who gathers around him?

answers.text: Everyone who trembled at God's words

cards.question: Ezra sits there in horror with people gathered around him. How long does he stay like that?

cards.text: At the evening offering, Ezra gets up with his clothes still torn, falls on his knees and spreads out his hands to the LORD his God. He tells God he's ashamed and embarrassed to even lift his face to Him.

cards.question: Ezra prays that their iniquities are higher than their heads, and their guilt has reached the ___.

cards.text: Higher than their HEADS. Friend, I spent years buried under takeout menus in a junk drawer, and Ezra's pile makes mine look like one sticky note.

cards.question: In his prayer, Ezra says Israel's great guilt only started with his own generation.

cards.text: From the days of their fathers to this day, Ezra says, their guilt has been great. Because of it, they and their kings and priests were handed over to the kings of the earth: sword, captivity, pillage and humiliation.
But then Ezra's prayer turns. He says that for a brief moment, grace has come from the LORD their God to preserve a remnant and give them a stake in His holy place.

cards.question: Even in their bondage, what does Ezra say God has given the people?

answers.text: New life and light to their eyes
A king and an army of their own

cards.text: Light to their eyes. Back in that junk drawer, one slice of kitchen light was the HIGHLIGHT of my whole week, so Ezra's got me over here nodding like a bobblehead.
Ezra says it straight: they are still slaves. But their God has not forsaken them in their bondage.

cards.question: Ezra says God has extended grace to His people in the sight of which kings?
Ezra says God's grace gives them new life to ___ the house of their God.

cards.text: On top of that, God's given them a wall of protection in Judah and Jerusalem. Then Ezra says, "And now, our God, what can we say after this?"

Ezra says they have forsaken the commandments God gave through His servants the prophets. Those commandments called the land they were entering polluted by the impurity of its peoples, filled with abominations from end to end.

cards.question: The commandments Ezra quotes say not to give their ___ in marriage to the sons of those peoples.
The commandments Ezra quotes tell Israel to seek the peace and prosperity of those peoples.
In the commandment Ezra quotes, why are the Israelites told to stay apart from those peoples?

answers.text: So they could be strong and pass the land on
So they could pay less to foreign kings
So they could rule over every nation

cards.text: Ezra looks back at everything that's come on them because of their evil deeds and their great guilt. And he admits something about how God has handled it.

cards.question: Ezra says God has punished them more than their iniquities deserve.

cards.text: God even left them a remnant like this one. So Ezra asks, shall they AGAIN break His commandments and intermarry with the peoples who commit these abominations?

cards.question: If the people break God's commandments again, what does Ezra ask whether God would do?

answers.text: Wipe them out with no survivor
Send them back down to Egypt
Give their land over to Moab

cards.text: Then Ezra comes to his last words. He calls out to the LORD, God of Israel.

cards.question: As Ezra ends his prayer, what does he say the LORD, God of Israel, is?
Ezra says that because of their guilt, no one can stand before God.

cards.text: Here they are before God in their guilt, still a remnant this day. And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because this story isn't done yet.

findings.problem: The passage opens with 'After these things had been accomplished,' which points back to Ezra 8. The card only says 'After everything's been done' and never says what those things were, such as Ezra's group arriving in Jerusalem and delivering the treasures and offerings (Ezra 8:32-36). The baker gets no context for where the passage picks up.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: 'I grabbed my mustache with BOTH hands' gives Papa Dorin hands. He has none. His mustache is what he uses as hands, so the joke breaks who he is.

rule.text: A cookie stamper with a huge French mustache that he uses as hands. He holds, points, waves and packs cookie boxes with it.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to finish the wording of Ezra's line ('our guilt has reached the ___'). The choices are heavens, mountains and rooftops. That tests exact wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This card repeats 'higher than their heads' from 9:6, which cards 12 and 13 already covered, and adds a joke. It tells nothing new, so it doesn't move the passage forward. It is a recap card with a joke on it.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: This card repeats 'light to their eyes' from 9:8, which card 2 just answered, and adds a joke. It tells nothing new from the passage. The joke should ride on a card that moves the passage forward.

rule.text: Every card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'abandon' is silly. 'God's grace gives them new life to abandon the house of their God' is not believable, so it is no real choice and points straight to 'rebuild.'

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'brothers' is not believable. 'Do not give your brothers in marriage to their sons' makes no sense, so it is no real choice next to 'daughters.'

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The line saying the story isn't over nearly copies the doc's example ('And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this story's not done.') instead of being written fresh.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: Except for the recap joke on card 3, stop 2 has no humor. Several moments could hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, like God punishing them less than they deserve (9:13) or Ezra asking 'what can we say after this?' (9:10). Papa Dorin reads like a plain narrator here, not the laugh-out-loud character his file describes.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
